Savannah by the numbers

Why does a Savannah house get two tax bills?

Georgia law makes a Savannah owner pay both city and county tax, and the two are mailed separately. The City of Savannah Revenue Department bills the city levy. The Chatham County Tax Commissioner bills county and school board taxes, as the city's calculation page explains.

  • City Revenue Department: 305 Fahm Street, 912-651-6455, weekdays 8:15 to 5. Mail: P.O. Box 1228, Savannah, GA 31402.
  • Chatham County Board of Assessors, 222 W. Oglethorpe Ave., Suite 113, 912-652-7271, for value, exemptions and appeals.
  • County Tax Commissioner: 912-652-7100.

The city does not value property. City Council picks the millage rate, and the county assessors pick the value it multiplies.

How big is Savannah, and who lives in its homes?

The 2020 count was 147,780 across 106.85 square miles of land. In QuickFacts the 2025 figure is 149,440, which works out to roughly 1,383 residents per square mile, spread over 58,192 households.

Tenants are the majority here, with owners in just 45.4 percent of homes. The midpoint owned home is valued at $248,900, midpoint rent is $1,382 and midpoint household income is $57,137. Commuters average 20.7 minutes, a third of adults (33.3 percent) have a four-year degree, and 7.6 percent of residents were born outside the country.

Landlords and investors therefore shape resale demand next to owner-occupants. Rental parcels pay tax without homestead relief, which makes their bills higher for the same value.

What is Savannah's millage rate?

A July 2026 news release from the city floated 11.749 mills for 2026, unchanged from 2025 and billed as the lowest since 1987. Its calculated rollback figure, the rate that would hold revenue flat after reassessment, stood at 11.402.

County, school board and other rates stack on top. The city says parcels covered by Stephens-Day are shielded from the extra bite that keeping the rate would otherwise pass along as values rise.

When do Savannah's installments come due?

The city splits real property into two bills. April brings the first, typically due in mid-June and equal to half of last year's tax. September brings the second, typically due mid-November, repriced for current value, exemptions and rate. The city warns that dates are fixed when bills print and can shift.

Chatham's own brochure, revised August 14, 2026, runs county real property on a different calendar: first bill mailed by April 1 for June 1, second mailed by September 15 for November 15. Personal property bills fall due by November 15.

Money has to be received and posted on or before the due date, so a mailing delay is your risk. The city takes partial payments through the second due date but arranges no payment plans. An unreceived bill is still owed; copies are online or at the Revenue Department counter.

What do late Savannah bills cost?

State law (O.C.G.A. 48-2-40 to 48-2-44) sets interest at bank prime plus 3 percent a year, added monthly. Four months late, a 5 percent penalty applies to all but small homestead bills, then again after each further four months until it totals 20 percent.

Left alone, an account becomes a fi. fa., a lien that hurts credit and can lead to a tax sale. The city runs roughly six sales a year, advertising each property four weeks before. After a sale the former owner has a year and a day to redeem by repaying the bid plus 20 percent.

While an appeal is open, the city bills at last year's value or 85 percent of the new one, whichever is lower, and collects at the second installment date. A corrected bill or a refund follows the ruling.

How do Stephens-Day and homestead exemptions work in Chatham County?

The house has to be your legal residence on January 1, owned and occupied. You can apply at any time of year, though the assessors must have it inside 45 days of the yearly assessment notice for the exemption to start that year. Matching addresses on a Georgia driver's license or ID and a vehicle registration are required, and staff may add a request for a prior utility bill or a voter card.

  • Standard homestead: $12,000 off the county side of assessed value, $2,000 off the school and state sides.
  • Stephens-Day, in place since 1999, and the statewide floating exemption both freeze a base year value. The owner gets whichever saves more.
  • Chatham senior exemption: for owners 65 and older whose net income does not exceed $10,000, it removes $30,000 from the county and school assessed value.

Sales, deed changes and significant improvements move the base. A bedroom addition raises the base by its added value, and a demolition lowers it by the value lost. Opting in or out of HB 581 leaves existing base years alone. Solid waste and street light fees still apply.

Does a short-term rental change my homestead position in Savannah?

Under the city's vacation rental ordinance, a parcel counts as owner-occupied only if the owner lives in its principal unit as their usual home. Applicants show that with a valid homestead exemption, or with a sworn affidavit plus two items of residency proof.

A homestead claim on a house that is really an investment rental is a problem waiting for a buyer's title review. Check your exemption status with the assessors before listing.

How can a Savannah owner appeal a Chatham County value?

Put the appeal in writing to the Chatham assessors inside 45 days of the notice, on the state's uniform form, and name your chosen method in that first filing. Valid grounds: taxability, value, uniformity, or an exemption that was denied.

  • Board of Equalization, with Superior Court review available afterward.
  • Arbitration, which needs a certified appraisal delivered inside those same 45 days. The assessors can take it or turn it down, and court review stays open.
  • Hearing officer, reserved for non-homestead real property of $500,000 or more, or certain wireless property over $200,000, on value or uniformity questions.

The brochure adds a relief for families: a surviving spouse or minor child may petition Probate Court for a year's support, within two years of a death, and an award can relieve tax for the year in the petition.

Where do I pay or ask questions in Chatham County?

County bills can be paid at tax.chathamcountyga.gov by card or eCheck; the eCheck is free and the card carries a convenience fee. Checks go to P.O. Box 9827, Savannah, GA 31412. Walk-in service is weekdays, 8:30 to 5, at three locations: W. Oglethorpe Ave., Police Memorial Dr. and Eisenhower Dr. Satellite desks on Wilmington Island Rd., US 80 and Georgia Highway 21 see people only by appointment.

County staff also bill for Garden City, Pooler, Port Wentworth, Thunderbolt, Tybee Island and Vernonburg. Any returned check is charged 5 percent of its amount, minimum $30. Tangible personal property other than vehicles, trailers and mobile homes is exempt when its total fair market value is $20,000 or less.

Can I sell a Savannah house that owes tax?

Yes. The title company collects payoff figures from the Revenue Department and the Tax Commissioner and settles both out of your proceeds. Any recorded lien turns up in the title search long before the closing date.

Cash offers avoid lender appraisals and repair lists. Compare each against a normal listing less repairs, back tax and holding costs.

More questions about Savannah, GA Property Tax Guide

Which office collects Savannah city property tax?

The city's Revenue Department takes it, at 305 Fahm Street, 912-651-6455. County and school taxes go to a different office, the Chatham County Tax Commissioner.

When does Savannah's second property tax bill come due?

Usually mid-November. Chatham's brochure names November 15 for county bills, and the city fixes its own date when it prints bills.

What is the appeal window in Chatham County?

Forty-five days after the annual notice of assessment, filed first with the Chatham County Board of Assessors.

What happens to a Savannah bill that is 120 days late?

A 5 percent penalty lands, on top of monthly interest at prime plus 3 percent a year, and it repeats each 120 days until it reaches 20 percent.

What does Stephens-Day do for a Chatham County owner?

A Chatham-only homestead exemption from 1999 that pins taxable value to a base year figure plus improvements. If the statewide floating exemption saves more, the owner receives that one.

Atlanta by the numbers

Which county bills me for property tax in Atlanta?

Fulton County bills most of the city, but Atlanta also extends into DeKalb County, so check which county your parcel sits in before you call anyone. Atlanta is the county seat of Fulton and spreads across the Fulton and DeKalb line, which means two assessors and two tax commissioners are involved citywide.

For Fulton parcels, the Board of Assessors sets the value and the Fulton County Tax Commissioner bills and collects for Fulton County, Fulton County and City of Atlanta Schools, the State of Georgia, and the City of Atlanta. Fulton has 18 taxing jurisdictions in all, each setting its own rate, and each is listed separately on the bill. For DeKalb parcels, the DeKalb Property Appraisal Department sets values, and its resource page gives the same 40 percent assessment ratio and a 45-day appeal window from the notice date.

  • Fulton Board of Assessors: 404-612-6440
  • Fulton Tax Commissioner: 404-613-6100, 141 Pryor Street SW
  • DeKalb Property Appraisal: 404-371-0841

When were Atlanta property taxes due in 2026?

City of Atlanta taxes were due September 30, 2026, and Fulton County taxes and those from all other jurisdictions were due October 15, 2026. Both dates have passed, and unpaid 2026 balances accrue interest.

2026 Fulton County property tax calendar (source: Fulton County press releases, June to August 2026)
EventDate
Assessment notices available onlineJune 19, 2026
Appeal deadline for most ownersJuly 31, 2026
Tax bills mailedAugust 15, 2026

Fulton's 2026 bills were temporary. A delay in sending the tax digest to the state meant the Superior Court of Fulton County authorized, on August 4, 2026, bills built on the preliminary 2026 digest and each jurisdiction's 2025 millage rate. Final rates are set once the state certifies the digest, and a refund or revised bill goes out only if needed.

Interest begins the day after the due date. An extra 5 percent penalty is added on the 120th day, and another 5 percent every 120 days after that, up to a maximum of 20 percent. The office accepts partial payments, though interest keeps accruing on the unpaid principal.

How do I pay an Atlanta property tax bill?

Pay online at fultoncountytaxes.org, by phone at 404-613-6100, by mail, or in person at the Tax Commissioner's office in the Fulton County Government Center, 141 Pryor Street SW. The office also operates three other full-service locations.

Mail goes to the Fulton County Tax Commissioner, 141 Pryor St. SW, Suite 1106, Atlanta, GA 30303. The office's website lets you search for a bill by parcel ID, account number or address, and it supports a multi-parcel summary lookup for owners with several properties. Credit card and e-check payments run through the same system. If an expected bill has not arrived by mid-September in a billing year, Fulton asks owners to call rather than wait.

Escrow does not remove the owner's responsibility. If your lender pays the tax, still confirm that the payment posted against the right parcel, particularly after a refinance or a servicer change.

What do I need to know about Atlanta's size, neighborhoods and housing?

The Census Bureau's 2025 estimate counts 529,110 residents across about 135 square miles of land, at an elevation near 1,050 feet. Owners are a minority: 46.4 percent of the 236,468 households own, per the 2020 to 2024 survey.

The middle owner-occupied home is valued at $439,600 and the middle monthly rent is $1,711. The city counts 242 officially defined neighborhoods. Three high-rise districts, Downtown, Midtown and Buckhead, run north to south along Peachtree, and most of the land between them is low-density single-family housing with a craftsman bungalow common in older areas.

  • Three interstates meet here: I-20, I-75 and I-85, with the Downtown Connector carrying more than 340,000 vehicles a day and I-285 mostly encircling the city as the Perimeter.
  • MARTA rail connects the airport, Downtown, Midtown and Buckhead.
  • Georgia Tech, Georgia State, Emory and the Atlanta University Center are among more than 15 colleges and universities in the city.
  • Atlanta annexed Emory into the city effective January 1, 2018.

Atlanta has a humid subtropical climate with about 50 inches of rain a year spread evenly through the seasons, and it is often called the City in a Forest for the density of its tree canopy.

How do I appeal an Atlanta assessment in Fulton County?

File within 45 days of the date on your Notice of Assessment, online at fultonassessor.org, in person at a Board of Assessors office, or by mail. For 2026, notices went out in June and the deadline for most owners was July 31, 2026, unless another date was printed on the notice.

The appeal covers the assessed value only, and the estimated tax cannot be appealed. Each appeal must pick one of three paths: a Board of Equalization hearing, non-binding arbitration on valuation, or a hearing officer, and the last two can carry fees. Hearings are held at 141 Pryor Street, Suite 2111, and the Board of Equalization office takes scheduling calls at 404-613-7792. Useful evidence includes the purchase price, an appraisal, photographs and comparable sales.

Either side can carry a Board of Equalization decision to Superior Court within 30 days of its mailing date. The appeals process can run for months, and Fulton warns that a temporary bill issued while an appeal is pending must still be paid or penalties apply. The 2026 notices also carried a new format under Senate Bill 566, with an Estimated Tax Savings section replacing the old estimated tax table.

  • Board of Assessors, Fulton County Center: 141 Pryor Street, Suite 1018
  • Customer Service Center: 11575 Maxwell Road
  • North Fulton Customer Service Center: 7741 Roswell Road NE, Suite 210
  • South Fulton Service Center: 5600 Stonewall Tell Road, Suite 224

All four are reached through the same assessor line, 404-612-6440.

What if I sell an Atlanta house while taxes are unpaid?

Plan to clear the balance through the closing, since unpaid Atlanta and Fulton tax follows the parcel. Georgia assigns a year's bill to whoever owned the home on January 1, and the state revenue department says there is no refund for a partial year if you sell and move.

Ask the Fulton Tax Commissioner for a payoff total that includes interest and any 5 percent penalty steps. The temporary billing used in 2026 adds one wrinkle: because a corrected bill or refund may follow once final rates are set, the closing attorney should agree in the contract how any later adjustment between buyer and seller will be handled.

A buyer's exemption starts fresh. Fulton's assessment announcement says owners who held the home on January 1 and missed the April 1 homestead deadline can still apply during the appeal period, while owners who bought after January 1 apply for the following tax year.

More questions about Atlanta, GA Property Tax Guide

Were Atlanta property tax bills final in 2026?

No. Fulton County issued temporary bills based on the preliminary 2026 digest and 2025 millage rates, as authorized by the Superior Court on August 4, 2026. A revised bill or refund follows only after final rates are set.

Is part of Atlanta in DeKalb County?

Yes. Atlanta is the seat of Fulton County and extends into DeKalb County. Parcels in the DeKalb part are valued by DeKalb Property Appraisal rather than the Fulton Board of Assessors, so confirm the county on your bill.

How many days do I have to appeal in Fulton County?

You have 45 days from the date of the Notice of Assessment. For most 2026 notices that ended July 31, 2026. After the deadline passes the right to appeal that year's value is lost.

How is a late Atlanta tax bill penalized?

Interest starts the day after the due date. A 5 percent penalty is added on the 120th day and again every 120 days, up to 20 percent total. Fulton accepts partial payments, but interest continues on what remains unpaid.

Which office do I call about my Atlanta home value?

For a Fulton County parcel, call the Board of Assessors at 404-612-6440. For billing or payment questions, call the Fulton Tax Commissioner at 404-613-6100. DeKalb parcels go to DeKalb Property Appraisal at 404-371-0841.

Columbus by the numbers

Who bills property tax in Columbus, Georgia?

Columbus and Muscogee County are one consolidated government, so one Tax Commissioner sends the bills and takes the payments for the whole city. The Muscogee County Board of Tax Assessors, whose members are appointed by City Council for fixed terms under state law, decides taxability and value.

The Tax Commissioner's site explains that City Council sets the mill rate for city operations and that the school board recommends its rate, which with few exceptions City Council must set for the schools. It adds that Georgia no longer has a state ad valorem tax, effective 2016. Citizens of Muscogee County appointed by the grand jury sit on the Board of Equalization, and the Clerk of Superior Court administers it.

  • Tax Commissioner: bills, collects, handles delinquent tax and tax sales.
  • Board of Tax Assessors: value, exemptions, appeals. The office help desk is 706-225-4398.
  • Board of Equalization: hears value, uniformity and exemption disputes.

The assessors' board meets Wednesdays at 9:00am in the City Services Building at 3111 Citizens Way.

What is Columbus like for a homeowner thinking of selling?

Columbus sits on the Chattahoochee River directly across from Phenix City, Alabama, about 100 miles southwest of Atlanta. It is Georgia's second most populous city and the seat of Muscogee County, and Wikipedia gives its area as roughly 221 square miles.

Fort Benning, south of the city, is the largest employer on the city's own 2025 employer list, followed by the Muscogee County School District, Piedmont Columbus Regional Hospital, Aflac and the city government. Columbus State University, Columbus Technical College and the headquarters of Aflac and Synovus also anchor the local economy. Interstate 185 runs through the middle of the city, and US 27, US 280 and SR 520 meet inside it.

Census QuickFacts shows a 2025 estimate of 202,171 residents, down 2.3% from the 2020 base. Owners live in just 50.8% of homes. A typical owned home is valued at $193,900, rent averages $1,106 and household income is $58,073. That renter-heavy mix means many Columbus sellers are landlords, and for a rental the tax bill still follows the January 1 owner.

What is the Columbus property tax calendar?

The Tax Commissioner posts a list organized by month. Assessment notices go out in May, bills arrive in August, and payment begins in October.

Columbus property tax dates from the Tax Commissioner
MonthWhat happens
April 1Mobile home bills due; homestead deadline; business personal property, aircraft and watercraft returns due
MayAnnual notice of assessment mailed; appeals within 45 days of the notice date
JulyTaxing authorities advertise and set millage rates
AugustReal and personal property bills mailed
OctoberBills due: a 40% installment or payment in full
DecemberRemaining 60% due

A homestead application can be filed in place of an appeal during the appeal window. The page does not print a day of the month for the October or December payments, so use the dates on your bill.

Does Columbus offer installments, and what does it mean for a closing?

Yes, the calendar above splits the bill into a 40% installment in October and the remaining 60% in December, or you may pay the full amount in October. A sale that closes between those payments needs the title company to know how much has already been paid.

The Tax Commissioner's buying and selling page states that the person who owns on January 1 is legally responsible for that year's tax, no matter who owns the house later. Both buyer and seller may get a bill, and the office does not decide who pays what share, since closing documents divide it.

If the tax goes unpaid, the lien lands on the January 1 owner unless the seller supplies proof inside 90 days of the due date that the buyer took over the liability. The page names a recorded deed in the new owner's name and closing language that clearly assigns the tax to the buyer as acceptable proof. Once verified, the lien may be recorded against the buyer.

Which Columbus homestead exemptions are listed?

The Tax Commissioner's list of types begins with the standard exemption, printed as a $13,500 reduction in assessed value, and then adds age, veteran and surviving-spouse exemptions. Apply at any time in the calendar year after the property becomes your primary residence, up to and including April 1 of the year you want the exemption.

  • Standard homestead (H1): $13,500 off assessed value, applying to the maintenance and operation levies of the county and school board, not bond debt.
  • Elderly general (H2): age 65 or older by January 1, with household net income not over $10,000 for the prior year, plus income documents.
  • Disabled veteran (H5): up to $121,812, shown as a 2025 figure, with a VA benefits letter.
  • Unremarried surviving spouse of a service member killed in a war or armed conflict: up to $121,812, with Department of Defense documents.
  • Surviving spouse of a firefighter or peace officer killed or fatally injured in duty: 100% exemption.

You need a copy of the recorded deed and a Georgia driver's license showing your current address, and voter and vehicle registration must be in Muscogee County. After approval the exemption renews until you move, the ownership changes or you seek a different one. A property tax deferral exists for owners 62 and older with gross household income of $15,000 or less, running until a change of ownership or until the deferred tax and interest reach 85% of fair market value.

What happens to unpaid Columbus property tax?

The Muscogee County Tax Commissioner can place a tax lien, called a fifa, and levy the property for a tax sale. The office does not sell its tax liens or lien certificates, and a property that fails to sell at a tax sale goes back into rotation for later sales. Its Delinquent Tax section includes a tax sale list and a class registration page for bidders.

The office's delinquent tax page says its staff cannot give legal advice and tells owners with a lien or levy to consult an attorney. For a seller, the practical sequence is simple: get the payoff from the Tax Commissioner, confirm it with the title company, and clear the lien from the sale proceeds if the house sells before a tax sale date.

Personal property has its own rule. Taxable tangible personal property other than motor vehicles, trailers and mobile homes is exempt when its total fair market value, as determined by the assessors, does not exceed $20,000.

How do I challenge a Columbus value?

Appeals are due 45 days after the date on the notice of assessment, which the Tax Commissioner's calendar places in May. The Board of Tax Assessors receives the appeal and reviews it, and the Board of Equalization hears matters of value, uniformity, taxability and denied exemptions.

The assessors' contact page gives separate channels: real property appeals go to ccgboa@columbusga.org, and personal property appeals to ppboa@columbusga.org. Questions about real property appeals can also go to 706-225-4398. A homeowner who has not yet claimed a homestead can file that application during the same appeal period instead of appealing.

Recent buyers and sellers of Columbus houses should keep the notice itself. It states the value the county will use for the bill, and the 45 days run from the date printed on it.

More questions about Columbus, GA Property Tax Guide

When are Columbus property tax bills due?

October, as either a 40% installment or payment in full, with the remaining 60% due in December. The Tax Commissioner's calendar does not print a day, so use the date on the bill.

Who is responsible for Columbus property tax after I sell?

The person who owned the property on January 1 is legally responsible for that year's tax. Closing documents normally divide it, and a lien moves to the buyer only with proof delivered within 90 days of the due date.

How much is the standard homestead exemption in Columbus?

The Tax Commissioner's page prints a $13,500 reduction in assessed value for the standard exemption. It applies to the county and school maintenance and operation levies, not the bond portion.

What is the appeal deadline in Columbus?

45 days from the date of the assessment notice, which the Tax Commissioner's calendar says is mailed in May. A homestead application can be filed in place of an appeal during that window.

Does the Columbus Tax Commissioner sell tax liens?

No. The office states it does not sell its tax liens or lien certificates. A property that does not sell at a tax sale returns to the rotation for future sales.

Augusta and Richmond County merged into one consolidated government on July 1, 1996, so county offices serve the whole city, though the separate towns of Blythe and Hephzibah stayed outside the merger and have their own tax districts.

The Tax Commissioner works from the Municipal Building at 535 Telfair Street, Suite 100, Augusta, GA 30901, with a mailing address of P.O. Box 1427, Augusta, GA 30903. The main line is 706-821-2391. The Board of Assessors answers value and appeal questions at 706-821-2310, and owners can look up their record and file an appeal online at augustarichmondtaxassessor.com.

  • Payments are accepted online, by mail, by phone at (706) 252-9080, in person at the Municipal Building, or at the South and West Augusta tag offices by debit card, credit card or check.
  • Every office has a drop box outside.
  • If a lender escrows your tax, the owner is still the one responsible for confirming payment.

When are Augusta property taxes due, and is there a discount?

Richmond County's 2026 bills were mailed September 30, 2026, with a due date of November 30. Owners who paid within the first 20 days, by October 20, 2026, received a 1 percent discount on the tax portion, which the county notes is offered by only a few Georgia counties.

After the due date, interest is added every month and a one-time 10 percent penalty is added in late December. Ask the office on 706-821-2391 for the exact monthly interest figure before paying a delinquent bill. Partial payments are accepted once bills are mailed, and penalties and interest continue on whatever remains.

An account with an outstanding balance is subject to a lien. Before a lien, known as a Fi.Fa., is issued, the office sends a 30-day notice of intent. Fi.Fa.s are recorded on the General Execution Docket of the Clerk of Superior Court, stay in effect for seven years, and may show up on credit reports. Paying the taxes, fees, penalties and interest cancels it.

What are the 2026 millage rates in Augusta-Richmond County?

The rate depends on which of four tax districts the house sits in. A mill is $1 of tax for every $1,000 of assessed value, and the tax is the assessed value, less exemptions, multiplied by the millage rate.

Two bodies set the rates that make up the total: the Richmond County Board of Commissioners and the Richmond County Board of Education. The tax commissioner says its office is only the billing and collection entity and has no role in setting amounts.

Voters approved a Floating Local Option Sales Tax (FLOST) on May 19, 2026. It is a 0.5 percent sales tax collected in Richmond County starting October 1, 2026, authorized for five years, and its proceeds must be used to reduce property taxes. The county says rollbacks show up on tax bills a year later, starting in 2027, and apply to a portion of the general county maintenance and operations levy.

What is it like to sell a house in Augusta?

Georgia's third-largest city, Augusta counted 201,999 residents in the Census Bureau's 2025 estimate and faces North Augusta, South Carolina, across the Savannah River. It covers more than 300 square miles, so density is only about 668 people per square mile.

Prices run far below Atlanta's. The typical owner-occupied home is valued at $178,400, half of the 75,222 households own (50.8 percent), and the typical monthly rent is $1,142. Median household income is $55,485.

  • Fort Gordon, Augusta University and the Savannah River Site are the three largest employers, and the Medical District employs more than 25,000 people.
  • The Masters Tournament brings more than 200,000 visitors to Augusta National each spring.
  • The Richmond County School System covers the whole county, with eight high schools and four magnet schools.
  • I-20 and I-520 (the Bobby Jones Expressway) are the main highways, about 148 miles from downtown Atlanta by I-20.

Augusta sits on the fall line between the Piedmont and the coastal plain, and the Augusta Canal begins at a diversion dam on the river. Winters are short and mild, summers are very hot, and Wikipedia records 82 days a year at or above 90 degrees.

How do I appeal an Augusta assessment or apply for a homestead exemption?

File within 45 days of the date on your assessment notice, and apply for a homestead exemption in the same window if you missed the earlier filing date. For 2026, notices mailed June 29 carried an August 13, 2026 deadline.

The notice is not a tax bill. It shows the assessed value, exemptions, and the right to appeal, and under Georgia Senate Bill 566 it now includes an Estimated Tax Savings section in place of the old estimated tax tables. Appeals can be filed online through the Property Search tool at augustarichmondtaxassessor.com, or by mail, email or in person. Augusta also has a local floating homestead exemption that limits certain increases in assessed value on qualifying primary residences.

Homestead applications go to the Tax Commissioner, which forwards them to the Board of Assessors for the final decision. A denial can be appealed to the Board of Equalization. The tax commissioner's site says an exemption renews automatically, and you do not have to apply again unless the ownership, name or deed changes. Refinancing does not affect it, and all vehicles owned by the applicant and spouse must be registered in Richmond County. When mailing an application, the office recommends certified mail, because metered postage dates are not accepted as timely.

What happens to Augusta property tax when I sell?

The January 1 owner carries that year's tax, and the purchase agreement can pass the liability to the buyer, which is usually settled at closing. The Richmond County Tax Commissioner advises people with questions to consult the closing attorney.

Bills still go out to the January 1 owner even if the property sold later in the year. If the seller is behind, ask the office for a current balance, which it says it updates nightly, and include the bill number or map and parcel number on any written request. A property can also show as under appeal or pending an assessment change order, in which case the bill may not yet be due, so confirm the status before paying.

If delinquent taxes lead to a tax sale, the county holds the auction on the first Tuesday of the month in the Commission Chambers of the Municipal Building at 535 Telfair Street, and it advertises the sale in the Augusta Chronicle for four consecutive weeks first. Selling before that point lets the closing pay the county from the proceeds.

What is the 2026 due date for Augusta property tax?

November 30, 2026. Bills were mailed September 30, and owners who paid within the first 20 days, by October 20, received a 1 percent discount on the tax portion. After November 30, monthly interest applies and a one-time 10 percent penalty follows in late December.

Is Augusta's property tax rate the same everywhere in Richmond County?

No. The county lists four tax districts for 2026: Urban at 28.284, County with fire at 26.28, Hephzibah at 24.939 and Blythe with fire at 26.839. The district printed on your bill decides the rate.

Did the 2026 assessment appeal window close?

Yes. For notices mailed June 29, 2026, the deadline was August 13, 2026. The right to appeal that year's value has ended, and the next window opens with the following year's notice.

What does FLOST do for Augusta homeowners?

FLOST is a 0.5 percent sales tax that began October 1, 2026, with proceeds used to cut property taxes. Rollbacks appear on tax bills starting in 2027, as a reduction to a portion of the county's general operating levy.

Who do I call about an Augusta property value?

Call the Richmond County Board of Assessors at 706-821-2310. For billing, payments or homestead questions, call the Tax Commissioner's office at 706-821-2391.

Why do Marietta owners open two tax envelopes every fall?

Two governments bill the same house. Cobb County mails a statement for county taxes. The City of Marietta Tax Division mails a second one that rolls up the city levy, Marietta City Schools, the Gateway Marietta Community Improvement District and the Downtown Marietta Development Authority. Paying one leaves the other untouched.

Value is the one thing the two share. Cobb's assessors decide it, and the city applies its own rates to that figure. Real property returns are filed with the Cobb assessors at 736 Whitlock Avenue, Suite 200.

  • Cobb statements go out by August 15 and are due October 15, either received or postmarked by the Postal Service. A metered or kiosk postmark is rejected.

  • The city calls a bill delinquent 60 days after mailing and sends it to the owner as of January 1.

The city's tax page describes Marietta's taxes as the lowest of any metro Atlanta city above 10,000 residents. Rates are reset each summer, so quote nobody's old number.

Where can I pay or ask a question in Marietta?

Walk into City Hall at 205 Lawrence Street, first floor, for the city's Tax Division, open from 8 am to 5 pm on weekdays. The phone is 770-794-5680, and a recorded line at 770-794-5130 runs day and night. A drop box at the City Hall parking deck is open at all hours. Online payment sits under How Do I on the city site, and the counter takes cards, checks, cash and money orders.

Cobb runs its main property tax office at 736 Whitlock Avenue and branches on Lower Roswell Road, Canton Road, Austell Road and Kemp Ridge Road. What kind of city is Marietta for a seller?

Marietta predates Atlanta. A plat was drawn in 1833, the legislature recognized the town on December 19, 1834, and the city incorporated in 1852. Like most Georgia towns, it grew around a square with a courthouse. The Western and Atlantic Railroad chose Marietta for its base, tanyards and taverns multiplied, and on April 12, 1862 the raiders of the Great Locomotive Chase boarded their train here. Union troops held the town in 1864 and burned it that November. The Marietta Museum of History sits on the second floor of the Kennesaw House.

The modern city is a dense, mostly renting one by Georgia standards. Census QuickFacts describe it this way.

  • A July 2025 population of 63,574, which is 4.1 percent above the April 2020 base of 61,060.
  • 23.43 square miles of land and 2,602 residents per square mile at the 2020 count.

  • Foreign-born residents at 18.1 percent, adults with a bachelor's degree or higher at 47.4 percent and residents 65 or older at 13.9 percent.
  • Household income of $72,725 at the median and a 27.5 minute average commute.

How do Marietta owners learn their value, and what is the appeal window?

Cobb's assessors mail notices before July 1. Treat the notice as an estimate, not a bill. It reports market value on January 1, shows the old and new values and estimates savings from approved exemptions, though the city warns that city exemptions may be missing from that estimate. The taxed share is 40 percent.

An owner has 45 days to appeal. The city's calendar uses the end of that window as a second deadline for homestead applications. While an appeal is open, Cobb Tax prints two amounts on the bill: the regular tax and a lower appeal amount based on 85 percent of assessed value or 100 percent of the prior value nobody contested. At least the appeal amount is due October 15. The City Tax Division offers an equivalent choice, paying the whole bill or 85 percent of it. If the final value lands after the due date, the owner pays any additional tax with interest.

A buyer files a first return with the Cobb assessors between January 1 and April 1 of the year after purchase. The city stresses that a lawyer does not file it. The assessors need a copy of the warranty deed and the owner's mailing address when it differs from the property address.

Which exemptions does a Marietta homeowner get?

Homestead exemptions apply to a house you own, live in and claim as your legal residence on January 1. The city says to apply by April 1 or within the 45-day appeal window, and only one name on the deed has to sign. Exemptions renew each year unless ownership changes, you stop qualifying or the city asks for a new filing. Apart from the veteran's exemption, the property has to be in the applicant's name, and a postmark on the deadline is enough.

Cobb describes a basic homestead exemption, senior exemptions that begin at age 62 and include a full or reduced school tax exemption, an exemption for 100 percent service-connected disabled veterans, and others for disabled owners, surviving spouses of certain public servants and some nonprofit and religious property.

  • City exemptions are handled by the Marietta Tax Division.
  • County exemptions are handled through Cobb.
  • A business can apply for a freeport inventory exemption with the Cobb assessors from January 1 to April 1, and the city grants a 100 percent exemption on qualifying inventory.

Once you sell, the exemption ends with your ownership. Cobb tells owners who lose eligibility to report it, using the form on the bill or its online request.

What does a late Marietta bill cost?

The city adds monthly interest on delinquent tax at the bank prime loan rate plus 3 percent, expressed as an annual rate that resets in January. A 5 percent penalty follows 120 days past the due date, and again every 120 days, to a maximum of 20 percent. A fi fa, the tax lien, adds its own charges.

Cobb also charges a 5 percent penalty and monthly interest, and says it cannot waive late fees. Its fi fa fee is $23 on taxes under $100 and $33 on taxes over $100, plus administrative costs. An owner who never receives a bill still owes the tax, and Cobb suggests printing the bill online.

Escrow can complicate things. When a mortgage servicer asks for the bill, Cobb sends one to both servicer and owner, and refunds a duplicate payment. The city copies the original to the servicer and a copy to the owner when notified in time. Verify which bill your escrow account actually paid.

How should I clear Marietta taxes before a sale?

In Marietta, taxes follow the property, so the current owner answers for anything outstanding. Call the Tax Division at 770-794-5680 for the city balance and Cobb Tax for the county balance, and ask both for written payoff figures and whether a lien has been filed.

After closing, report the sale and your new mailing address to Cobb in writing. The city says it is your job to contact the Tax Division if an expected bill never shows up.

More questions about Marietta, GA Property Tax Guide

What are the Marietta property tax due dates?

Cobb County bills are due October 15. City of Marietta bills, mailed from late August, were due October 31 for 2026. Check the date printed on each bill.

Which office bills the City of Marietta tax?

The City of Marietta Tax Division, at 205 Lawrence Street, 770-794-5680. Its bill covers the city, Marietta City Schools, Gateway Marietta CID and the downtown authority.

Who hears a Marietta value appeal?

The Cobb County Board of Tax Assessors receives it, inside 45 days of the notice. The city does not set value and sends valuation questions to the Cobb assessors.

Can I pay less while my appeal is pending?

Yes. The city allows 85 percent of the billed amount by the due date, and Cobb prints a lower appeal amount to be paid by October 15. Interest can apply if the final value arrives later.

Does the buyer or the seller owe the Marietta tax bill?

The tax follows the property, and the current owner is responsible for what is outstanding. Bills go to the January 1 owner, so the sale contract should say who reimburses whom.

Who sends a property tax bill to a Smyrna homeowner?

Two governments do. Cobb County bills county and school taxes through the Cobb County Tax Commissioner, and the City of Smyrna sends its own separate city bill. Many owners expect one statement and miss the second, so confirm both before you list a house or sign a contract.

The county's tax estimator page says its figures cover county taxes only and tells city residents to contact their municipal tax office. Smyrna's city tax department sits at City Hall, 2800 King Street, and its Property Tax page says occupational taxes are collected separately through business license renewals and that the city imposes no municipal sales tax.

When are Smyrna and Cobb County property taxes due?

The two bills run on different calendars. Cobb mails its bills by August 15 to the January 1 owner and sets the due date at October 15. Smyrna issues its bills in September and puts the due date in November.

What homestead exemptions can a Smyrna owner claim?

Smyrna homeowners can ask for exemptions from both governments, and each one is filed with its own office. The city lists these:

Cobb County's separate list includes a $10,000 basic homestead exemption that carries a $2,000 state component, an age 62 school tax exemption, an age 65 exemption with an income limit of $10,000, and a state tax exemption for owners 65 and older on the home and up to 10 acres. Cobb says every qualification must be met as of January 1, and city residents file city exemptions at the city tax office.

How do I pay Smyrna property tax, and what if I fall behind?

The city lists these ways to pay:

  • Online at smyrnaga.gov, by e-check or card.
  • By phone at 877-765-7651.
  • By mail to Attn: Tax Department, PO Box 1226, Smyrna, GA 30081.
  • In person on the second floor of City Hall.

Online card or debit payments carry a fee of the greater of $2.50 or 3.5%, e-checks carry $1.95, and in-person check or cash payments carry no added fee, per the city page.

The city's FAQ says unpaid bills accrue penalties and interest and that a FIFA lien is recorded with the Cobb County Clerk of Superior Court against the property address and the owner. The FAQ adds that this lets the city collect before a sale can occur. Ask the Smyrna Tax Department for a payoff figure in writing before a closing date is set.

How can I appeal a Smyrna assessment?

Cobb County's assessment notice carries the appeal deadline, and the Cobb tax commissioner points owners to that notice for the date. Homestead applications are also tied to it: Cobb says an application must be postmarked or received before the appeal deadline on the Notice of Assessment, and applications that come later are processed for the following year.

Cobb's property tax page says it also processes tax sales, mobile homes, boats and aircraft, and prepares the annual tax digest. The assessor's office, a separate office, handles valuation questions and appeals.

What does the Census say about Smyrna homeowners?

The Census Bureau's QuickFacts estimate puts Smyrna at 57,513 residents on July 1, 2025. The 2020 to 2024 survey figures show an owner-occupied rate of 59.4%, a median owner-occupied home value of $449,500, median gross rent of $1,739 and 24,809 households. Median household income is $100,061.

With 15.56 square miles of land and about 3,578 people per square mile, the city is a compact, built-up place. Smyrna calls itself the Jonquil City, was incorporated in 1872, and has a downtown anchored by the Market Village and Village Green near City Hall.

How does Smyrna calculate the city tax on a house?

The city's FAQ prints the method: take the total appraised value, multiply by 40%, subtract exemptions, multiply by the millage rate, and divide by 1,000. Each owner's exemptions differ with eligibility, so two neighbors with the same appraisal can receive different city bills.

The same FAQ states that the 62 and older exemption, the totally disabled exemption and the floating homestead exemption apply only while the owner lives at the property that receives them. Ask the Smyrna Tax Department what a buyer must file after closing, since the owner's residence is a condition of each exemption.

Cobb County's tax estimator covers county taxes only and tells city residents to contact their municipal tax office for city figures. The estimator is for a single tax year and is not a bill, so rely on the official bill when you negotiate a credit.

What is Smyrna's setting and history?

Cobb County was once split between the State of Georgia and the Cherokee, until an 1831 settlement deeded the land to Georgia. A campground was permanently established in 1832, and the place was known as Ruffs Siding and then Varners Station before taking the name Smyrna. Railroad construction through Cobb ran from 1836 to 1842 and gave the settlement a permanent location.

The city's first brick building went up in 1850 as a boys' academy, and the State incorporated Smyrna in 1872. A house within a short walk of that district is a different product from one on the city edge, and the city's parcel search map shows zoning for a given lot.

What city rules matter if I repair or rent a Smyrna house before selling?

The city's Building Division requires permits for roofs, windows, decks, interior remodeling, pools, generators, solar panels, demolition and any project with two or more licensed trades. General building permits are $7.00 per $1,000 of construction cost plus a 10% records fee and a $15.00 technology fee, with a $125.00 minimum, as the city prints it. Residential plan review typically takes 5 to 10 business days, and all applications go through the online portal.

A homeowner can pull a permit only for a permanent residence listed in the owner's legal name, and the city says a landlord working on a rental must be a Georgia-licensed contractor. Short-term rental licenses come from the Business License Division, and Code Enforcement handles complaints such as high grass and debris. Call Community Development at (678) 631-5387 about open permits.

More questions about Smyrna, GA Property Tax Guide

Does Smyrna have its own property tax?

Yes. The City of Smyrna issues its own bill, separate from the Cobb County bill. Its Property Tax page says city bills go out in September and are due in November, and the city's FAQ states the city millage rate has been 8.99 mills since fiscal year 2008.

Where do I file a Smyrna city homestead exemption?

File with the City of Smyrna Tax Department by April 1. The city accepts forms by mail to 2800 King Street, by fax at (770) 431-2814, by upload, or in person at City Hall. For questions call (678) 631-5325.

When is the Cobb County property tax bill due for a Smyrna address?

October 15. Cobb mails bills by August 15 to the January 1 owner and requires a U.S. postmark or receipt by the deadline, with metered and kiosk postmarks not accepted. The city's separate bill is due in November.

Can I sell a Smyrna house if the city tax bill is unpaid?

Yes, but the city can record a FIFA lien at the Cobb County Clerk of Superior Court, and its FAQ says that lien lets the city collect before a sale occurs. Get a payoff from the Smyrna Tax Department and have it paid at closing through your closing attorney.

Do rental houses in Smyrna get the city homestead exemption?

No. The city's exemption page says its homestead exemptions apply only to residential property that is the owner's primary residence, and rental properties do not qualify.

  • A bill that never arrives does not excuse a late payment, because the county mails to the last known address.

When were Athens property taxes due for 2026?

Athens-Clarke County mailed its 2026 bills on August 20, 2026, and payment was due by October 20, 2026. That date has passed, and any balance left open after it accrues interest and penalties.

The tax division describes October 20 as the usual date for real estate and business personal property. Late balances carry a 5 percent penalty every 120 days past the due date, up to four times, for a total of 20 percent. Interest also runs on the unpaid amount. The county says Georgia law requires late fees for any bill not paid by the deadline.

Money from the bill goes to the Clarke County Board of Education, the unified government and the State of Georgia. The county's 2026 budget ordinance sets the general fund rate at 12.25 mills, and a separate 1 mill levy applies to real property in the downtown area under the Downtown Development Authority.

What is the housing market like in Athens for a seller?

Athens is a college town where tenants outnumber owners, and that shapes who shops for a house. Census figures for 2020 to 2024 show 40.7 percent of households owning, out of 53,643 households in all. The middle owner-occupied home is worth $299,200, and the middle gross rent is $1,219 a month.

The University of Georgia anchors the economy, and Athens Technical College adds a second campus. Public schools belong to the Clarke County School District, and private choices include Athens Academy and Athens Christian School. Wikipedia places downtown Athens about 70 miles northeast of downtown Atlanta, and lists technology firms and pharmaceutical manufacturers among local employers.

  • The city sits on Piedmont hills, with annual rainfall near 46 inches and about 48 days a year at or below freezing.
  • US 78, US 441 and the SR 10 Loop carry most traffic, and Broad Street and Milledge Avenue cross the city.
  • The 2025 Census estimate is 128,612 residents, and the 2020 count worked out to about 1,094 per square mile.

Most trips in the city run on US 78 (Broad Street and Atlanta Highway), US 441 and Milledge Avenue, and the Athens-Ben Epps Airport had no scheduled airline service as of 2025, so most travelers drive to Atlanta. Athens voters approved a merger of the old city with Clarke County in 1990, and the unified government took effect in 1991, which is why a single tax office covers addresses that were once inside and outside the former city limits.

How do I file a property tax return or appeal in Athens-Clarke County?

A real estate return on form PT-50R goes to the Tax Commissioner in courthouse Room 250 during the first three months of any year in which the property changed hands or was improved, with April 1 as the last day. Owners with no changes may skip the return. Missing a required return brings a 10 percent penalty on the unreturned value, plus interest.

Business equipment and other personal property must be returned to the Board of Assessors every year by April 1. Challenges to a value or a denied exemption start with the Board of Assessors, and the county says an appeal that ends without agreement moves automatically to the Board of Equalization. The Assessors' office also notes that its staff inspect properties with active building permits, recent sales and open appeals, and that the notice period for those visits runs through December 31, 2026.

The state allows 45 days from the day the assessment notice is mailed. In Athens that same window also closes the door on homestead applications, so one date does double duty.

What homestead exemption does Athens-Clarke County give?

The standard Athens exemption removes $2,000 at the state level, $25,000 from the county maintenance and operations levy and $10,000 from the school levy. Athens-Clarke County says its local exemption for the county portion rose to $25,000 as of 2023.

The home must be your owner-occupied main residence at the start of the year. Applications are made in person at the Tax Commissioner's office, and the deadline is the same 45-day window used for appeals, typically opening with notices mailed in mid-May. The 2026 application deadline was July 6, 2026. Miss it, and the exemption waits for the next tax year.

  • A low-income exemption and several age-based and veteran exemptions exist for qualifying owners.
  • A one-time Homeowners Tax Relief Grant appears only on the 2026 bill, not on the assessment notice.

What happens to my Athens tax bill if I sell this year?

Even after a sale, the bill goes to whoever owned the home when the year began. The county's own notice tells new owners to call the Tax Commissioner for payment instructions and tells sellers who received a bill after selling to call so the account does not turn up as delinquent.

The tax division also tells buyers to verify before closing that no taxes are owed, because attorneys check real estate balances but can overlook personal property such as boats or business equipment. A seller who owes back taxes should phone 706-613-3120 for a payoff total and hand it to the title company, which can settle the account out of the proceeds.

Georgia's revenue department adds that no refund is available for a partial year of ownership. Unpaid taxes that reach the collection stage can lead to levy and sale of the property, according to the county's tax division. Selling before that point keeps the sale in your control and the balance in the closing statement.

More questions about Athens, GA Property Tax Guide

How much is the Athens-Clarke County millage rate?

The 2026 budget ordinance sets the general fund rate at 12.25 mills for Athens-Clarke County government. Downtown real property carries an extra 1 mill levy, and school and state levies are billed separately on the same statement.

Where can I mail an Athens property tax payment?

Mail it to the Tax Commissioner at PO Box 1768, Athens, GA 30603. You can also pay online at athensclarketax.com, in person in courthouse Room 250 or in a drop box, using checks or money orders only in the drop box.

Did the 2026 Athens bill include any one-time credit?

Yes. The county says a one-time Homeowners Tax Relief Grant is applied to 2026 bills for each qualifying homestead. It shows up on the tax bill, not on the assessment notice, so do not look for it on the notice.

Do I need a new homestead application if I add someone to the deed?

Yes. The county says an approved exemption stays in place while you own and occupy the home, but a change in ownership, such as adding a spouse to the deed or moving the home into a trust, requires a new application.

Which number do I use to question my Athens value?

Phone the Assessors at 706-613-3140, then put the appeal in writing within 45 days of the notice date. Without an agreement, the county sends it on to the Board of Equalization.

How did a farm stop called Wellston become Warner Robins?

A railroad stop with a sawmill, a grocery and peach orchards, Wellston held only about 50 people in 1940. Houston County mails real estate statements ahead of October 20, and December 20 is the due date. The office accepts partial payments. Interest builds each month at the legal rate, and every 120 days adds a 5% penalty until the penalties reach 20%.

Statements are mailed to the homeowner and never to the lender. Borrowers who escrow need to send the bill along themselves.

  • Real property returns and conservation-use requests: mailed, with a postmark of April 1 at the latest.

To challenge a value, write to the Board of Tax Assessors within 45 days of the notice. From there the path runs through the Board of Equalization (or arbitration) and, if needed, Superior Court. Complaints about the size of the bill are outside the appeal.

Call the commissioner's Warner Robins office for a payoff and hand the figure to your closing attorney or title company. Value is fixed as of January 1 each year, so the sale contract should state how the year's bill is divided.

Landlords should check personal property too. The assessors warn that people who buy a business, boat or aircraft sometimes find years of unpaid tax afterward, and that attorneys usually review only the real estate side.

The state homestead exemption knocks $2,000 off the assessed value, which itself is 40 percent of market value. Returns are due from January 1 to April 1, and a taxpayer who skips one is treated as repeating last year's return. Alpharetta takes its own homestead filing, so confirm that both the city and the county list your exemption.

At the 2020 census Alpharetta had 65,818 residents in 24,727 households, with 26,089 housing units. Fulton County Schools serve the city, and Alpharetta High School covers most of it. What happens to the tax bill at an Alpharetta closing?

The owner on January 1 carries the year's tax, with no partial-year refund. Transfer tax comes due before the deed is recorded, the seller is the liable party unless the contract says otherwise, and the PT-61 form is filed online with the state's clerks' cooperative.

County tax liens are recorded on the general execution docket at the clerk's office. Before listing, request a balance statement from the Tax Commissioner and from the city, and ask whether any 2026 estimated payment remains open.

The Tax Commissioner's office combines the assessors' value and exemption data with millage rates from the county commission and other governing bodies, then mails bills to the address the assessors hold. For walk-in help, Maxwell Road is nearest. The county also lists a downtown Atlanta office at 141 Pryor Street SW, Suite 1113, and a North Fulton Service Center at 7741 Roswell Road NE in Sandy Springs, each on the 404-613-6100 line.

Can I recover tax paid by mistake?

That matters for the 2026 temporary bills, which rested on 2025 millage rates and a partial digest. The county's announcement says a revised bill or refund may follow. Hold on to the receipt for any estimate payment and compare it with the final bill before closing.

Georgia separately taxes recording of a long term real estate note, at $1.50 per $500 of face amount or part of $500, and the security instrument must be recorded within 90 days. Ask the Clerk of Superior Court who collects it in Fulton County.

Not always, and the answer decides which offices bill you. Alpharetta's northeast edge touches unincorporated Forsyth County, and its other borders are Milton, Roswell and Johns Creek, each with its own city government.

Schools show the same overlap. How do I contest an Albany value?

File in writing with the Board of Assessors inside the 45 day window. Georgia supplies a uniform form, and the grounds can include value, uniformity, taxability or a denied exemption.

That first filing also names the route, which is the Board of Equalization, a hearing officer or an arbitrator. The state revenue department cannot overrule these bodies on a single parcel. Bring any comparable sales, repair estimates and photographs you want considered.

What exemptions and special assessments exist in Dougherty County?

The statewide homestead exemption takes $2,000 off assessed value, and the tax is that reduced value times the millage rate. Assessed value runs 40 percent of market value. Apply by April 1 of the first year you want it, since skipping the application waives the exemption. Ask the Tax Department about any local additions.

Dougherty County also offers special assessments through the Board of Assessors:

  • Preferential agricultural assessment, which values qualifying farm property at 30 percent of fair market value rather than 40 percent.
  • Conservation use assessment for certain agricultural, timber, environmentally sensitive and transitional residential land, valued at current use.
  • Forest land protection exemption for land used mainly for growing trees and timber.

Conservation applicants commit to ten years of qualifying use and may enroll at most 2,000 acres statewide. Anyone selling an enrolled tract should ask the Board of Assessors what the sale does to the commitment.

What should an Albany seller know about taxes at closing?

Whoever held title on January 1 owes the year's tax, and the state allows no refund to a partial year owner, so the contract and closing statement divide the bill.

The transfer tax runs $1 for the first $1,000 (or fraction) and 10 cents for each added $100 (or fraction) of price. The deed's signer is liable, though a contract may hand it to the buyer. Payment comes before recording at the Clerk of Superior Court, with the PT-61 declaration filed online through the state clerks' cooperative.

A home near the Flint River raises a flood question. The river damaged property in 1841 and 1925, Tropical Storm Alberto brought a severe flood in 1994, and the river crested at 35 feet above its bed in 1998. The city decided against redeveloping parts of its riverfront floodplain. Ask city staff about floodplain status for a given address.

What else shapes an Albany house sale besides the tax bill?

The largest employers in town are health care, education and the Marine Corps Logistics Base Albany, followed by manufacturing, transportation and retail. Phoebe Putney Memorial Hospital anchors the regional health system, Albany State University and Albany Technical College sit inside the city, and the Dougherty County School System runs the public schools.

No interstate serves Albany. Two U.S. highways, 19 and 82, run through, and the Liberty Expressway loops the north and east. In January 2017 an EF3 tornado hit the south side, and in October 2018 Hurricane Michael tracked through south Georgia. If your house had storm repairs, keep the damage history, permits and receipts together.

Whatever the condition, the tax paperwork has the same parts: the Tax Department's bill for the parcel, the Board of Assessors' value and exemption record, and the transfer tax certification the Clerk of Superior Court attaches to the deed.

How is Albany run, and who supplies the services a buyer asks about?

Albany's city government is a commission and manager system that has been in place since January 14, 1924: a mayor, six commissioners elected from single-member districts, and an appointed city manager who runs daily operations. The city was incorporated on December 27, 1838, on ground the Creek people called Thronateeska, their word for flint. Steamboats and then seven railroad lines made it a trading center, and the Turner Air Force Base years brought a large military presence until the base closed in 1974 and the land went back to the city.

A buyer will ask about utilities. Albany Water, Gas & Light, a municipal commission, supplies water, gas and electricity to its customers, although parts of Albany are served by Georgia Power. The public water supply comes from four aquifers. The city reports a fire protection rating of ISO 2, and the county landfill on Gaissert Road handles solid waste. Albany Transit System buses connect the city and the county, and Southwest Georgia Regional Airport offers service to Atlanta.

Public safety splits by territory. The Albany Fire Department operates 11 stations in Dougherty County, seven of them inside the city limits, and the Albany Police Department is organized into three districts, each with its own police center. The Dougherty County Police Department covers the unincorporated area. The city also has a tree ordinance and a certified arborist on staff, so ask the city before removing a large tree.

More questions about Albany, GA Property Tax Guide

Who do I call about a delinquent Albany property tax bill?

Ring the Dougherty County Tax Department at 229-431-3208. One bill covers all four levies.

Is there a separate City of Albany bill?

No. The county department folds city tax into the same bill as county, school and state tax.

What is the deadline to dispute an Albany value?

Forty-five days from the mailing of the assessment notice, filed in writing with the assessors.

Does the $18,000 grant reach a rental in Albany?

It goes only to homesteads with a qualifying 2026 exemption, which rules out rentals and vacant houses.

Who owes transfer tax on an Albany sale?

State law makes the seller liable, and the contract may reassign it.

Which office bills a Macon property owner?

The Macon-Bibb County Tax Commissioner sends the bill, and the proceeds go to the State of Georgia, Macon-Bibb County and the Board of Education. Macon-Bibb's commissioners and the school board vote the millage rates. Values are the Tax Assessors' job.

  • Tax Commissioner: phone 478-621-6500, email taxinfo@maconbibb.us, website maconbibbtax.us. It bills, collects, distributes the money and prepares the digest for the state each year.
  • Board of Tax Assessors: 688 Walnut Street, Suite 200, Macon, GA 31201, phone (478) 200-5550, website bibbassessors.com.
  • Deed room at the Macon-Bibb County Courthouse, 601 Mulberry St., for copies of a warranty deed.

The tax commissioner's FAQ stresses that the office is an independent elected one, separate from the assessors and from the county commissioners. Send value questions to the assessors and payment questions to the commissioner.

How does the Macon-Bibb housing picture compare with other Georgia counties?

Macon-Bibb County has the biggest population of the four Georgia places compared here, an estimated 157,556 in mid-2025. Against the 157,358 estimates base for 2020, that is a gain of just 0.1%.

With a land area of 249.38 square miles and a 2020 density of 630.9, Macon-Bibb is far more crowded than Lowndes, Lumpkin or Long County. Owners live in 51.4% of homes, the lowest share of the group, and the midpoint price of those homes is $174,500 in the 2020 through 2024 data. Median gross rent runs $1,066, and the county counts 59,921 households.

Half of households bring in less than $51,234, and a quarter of residents (24.7%) are below the poverty line. Retail sales in 2022 totaled about $5.87 billion, or $37,595 per resident, the highest by a wide margin of the four places, with medical and social service receipts near $2.45 billion.

What dates matter on a Macon property tax bill?

Macon-Bibb splits the bill on land, buildings and personal property into two installments. Weekend dates slide forward.

Macon-Bibb County property tax calendar from the tax commissioner and the assessors
ItemDate or rule
Statements for land, buildings and personal property mailedBy September 15
First installment dueOctober 15
Second installment dueNovember 15
Property returnsFiled by April 1
Homestead applicationReceived before April 1 to apply that year
Mobile home statements go outBy January 30
Mobile home tax deadlineApril 1
Garbage charge, each quarterMarch 31, June 30, September 30, December 31

Source: the tax commissioner's property and FAQ pages, plus the assessors' return deadline page.

A postal-service postmark with a date shows a current-year payment was on time. A date from a postage meter does not qualify. Partial payments are welcome, but interest and penalties keep running on what remains. Millage rates are announced each year in late July or early August, once the commissioners and the Board of Education approve them.

Why is a garbage fee tied to Macon property tax?

Every residential premises meant for occupancy, vacant or not, is billed for garbage service, and the Solid Waste Department's service is mandatory. The tax commissioner's page says garbage is now billed quarterly, with due dates at the end of each quarter.

  • Appealing a property value does not pause the garbage fee, which stays due in full.
  • Owners with income under the federal poverty guidelines may seek an exemption, with with applications turned in at the Solid Waste Department, 327 Lower Poplar St., before the 5:00 p.m. cutoff on November 1 of each year.
  • If a home is destroyed by fire or casualty or demolished, the owner must notify the Solid Waste Director in writing right away.

Solid Waste handles service questions at 478.803.0499 or garbage@maconbibb.us. Ask the commissioner whether a garbage charge is open when you request a payoff.

How do returns, homestead and appeals work for a Macon owner?

To get a value review, an owner has to file a return by April 1. The assessors say skipping it blocks any review. Returns go to the Tax Assessors' Office, which mails a notice when it disagrees with your figure.

You have a 45 day window beginning with the notice date. The written appeal starts with the Board of Assessors and has to name the method you choose. Call the assessors before you file if you are unsure how to proceed.

Homestead applications are approved by the Tax Assessors' Office. Eligibility turns on January 1, when you must be both owner and resident. An application in hand before April 1 counts for that year, and a move or a deed change calls for a fresh one. Mobile home owners who dispute the assessed value get the later of two deadlines: 45 days after the bill is mailed, or April 1.

What happens if Macon property tax goes unpaid?

State law attaches interest and penalties to any tax left unpaid beyond the due date. Before the office issues a lien (FiFa), it mails a notice of intent giving 30 days to pay in full. Mobile homes paid late face a state-mandated penalty of 10 percent or $5.00, whichever is greater, plus monthly interest.

  • Sales happen at 11 AM on the courthouse steps at the United Building in Central City Park, 206 7th Street, on the first Tuesday of any month with a sale on the calendar.
  • The winning bidder buys a Sheriff's Tax Deed, pays within two hours, and can use cash, certified funds or money orders only.
  • Redemption by the owner is open for 12 months, at a price that can include the bid, later taxes the buyer paid, special assessments and a 20% premium.
  • The buyer cannot cut off that right until a year after the sale.

Money from a sale beyond the taxes and costs is called excess funds, and the commissioner holds it. A mortgage company or lienholder may claim it before the owner, and the page says competing claims can end up in Superior Court.

What follows a Macon-Bibb tax sale for the old owner and the buyer?

A sale list, when one is scheduled, runs in The Telegraph's legal advertisements every Tuesday for four weeks beforehand. Anyone curious about a delinquent property that is not on a list can ask for the Levy Department at 478-621-6500. The opening bid is the tax due plus penalties and fees, and extra costs for title research and advertising are added once a property is picked for sale.

The winning bidder holds a Sheriff's Tax Deed rather than a clean title, and Georgia law bars the buyer from taking possession, making improvements or evicting tenants right away. To cut off the owner's right to redeem once the 12 months pass, the buyer has to send certified mail to the record owner and every interest holder, then run a newspaper notice weekly for four straight weeks. A quiet title petition comes next, and the court appoints a Special Master to decide who was owed notice.

Macon-Bibb County does not assist with redemption or its foreclosure, so an owner facing a sale should get professional advice quickly.

How does selling a Macon house with tax due work?

Whoever is on record as owner at the start of the year gets the bill. When a transfer is reported to the office within the 90 days leading up to the due date, the new owner is billed instead. Ownership data comes from deeds recorded at the courthouse and relayed by the assessors.

If you close between billing and the due dates, ask the commissioner at 478-621-6500 for a payoff that covers both installments. Lenders with escrow accounts get a data file, yet paying the tax remains the owner's job.

Boats, aircraft and business equipment work the same way: whoever owned the item at New Year's owes the full year, even after a sale or a relocation, and the assessors want proof before they remove the account.

More questions about Macon, GA Property Tax Guide

Which installment dates apply to Macon property tax?

October 15 and November 15, after statements are mailed by September 15. A weekend date moves forward.

Which number reaches the Macon tax office?

The Macon-Bibb County Tax Commissioner answers at 478-621-6500. For value questions, the Board of Tax Assessors lists (478) 200-5550 on its own site.

Does Macon accept postmarks on mailed property tax payments?

Yes, but only a dated postal-service postmark counts toward the current year's tax, not a meter stamp.

When is the Macon homestead exemption deadline?

The office needs it before April 1 for it to count that year, and you have to hold and occupy the home on January 1.

When are Macon-Bibb tax sales held?

At 11 AM on the first Tuesday of a month with a sale scheduled, on the steps at the United Building in Central City Park. A bidder or representative has to be present.
